note: 8개 기준별 부족한 점 분석(analysis)과 확인(check: 우리 쪽은 코드·문서, 경쟁 앱 쪽은 저장된 출처·당일 검색). 사람이 읽는 정리는 docs/review-competitors.md.

analysis.dimension: Design: what you see — brand and identity, typography, colour, icons and illustration, data visualisation, polish
analysis.standing: dulset has a better visual foundation than most prototypes: a warm paper-and-espresso palette that is not pink, a complete and tuned dark mode, measured contrast, and a consistent 56-icon line set. It does not yet look like a store-grade consumer app, because emoji stand in for people and icons, no typeface or wordmark is shipped, half the text is 12.5px or smaller, and every screen is a stack of slightly different cards. The weakest screens are the husband's (his home and the partner link): three to four screens of small text with no single dominant thing, which is the opposite of the positioning.

ahead.point: The brand colour is deliberately not pink, coral or purple: warm paper with an espresso fill, and period red and fertile violet are each reserved for one meaning. A husband can open it without it reading as a women's-health app.
ahead.versus: 핑크다이어리 (분홍 계열), ルナルナ (분홍·흰색), Flo (pink/coral), Premom (코랄·분홍), 마미톡 (분홍·코랄), Glow (보라). Most of these colours are from researcher memory, not screenshots. Clue is the one rival that also dropped pink. Caveat: our welcome mark and avatar circles bring blue/pink back.
ahead.evidence: app/globals.css (tokens with contrast figures), tailwind.config.ts, AGENTS.md code rule (theme tokens only, no hex or gray-*)

ahead.point: Dark mode is complete and tuned rather than inverted, and accessibility basics are measured: lowest text contrast 4.67:1 light and 4.90:1 dark across 13 screens, no unnamed controls on four tabs, calendar states use pattern as well as colour, with forced-colors and reduced-motion rules.
ahead.versus: Clue rebuilt its colour system and calendar for low-vision users and Natural Cycles has a dark-mode toggle; dark mode and contrast could not be confirmed for Flo or the Korean trackers. This puts us level with the leaders that declare accessibility, except for Larger Text (our sizes are fixed px).
ahead.evidence: app/globals.css; design audit 'accessibility' and 'dark_mode' in the digest; ours/shots/10-her-home-dark-vp.png

ahead.point: No ad or shop surface anywhere in the visual hierarchy; the home is content only.
ahead.versus: 핑크다이어리 (full-screen popup ad on open, bottom banner on every surface, calendar date sticker ads), 베이비빌리 (splash banner and main popup sold as ad products, point missions), 마미톡 (splash ads; reviews say '광고가 너무 심해진다'), 해피문데이 커넥트 ('선물하기' tab on the partner's app).
ahead.evidence: AGENTS.md ('분석·광고 SDK와 외부 폰트는 추가하지 않아요'), docs/STATUS.md 2026-09-29 rule ('오늘 화면에는 광고를 넣지 않아요'), docs/positioning.md §6

ahead.point: Privacy is visible in the drawing itself: his 주기 tab is a narrower picture (one violet tint, no period or LH marks, 1134px against her 2215px), she can preview his screen, the cover never shows health words, and the KakaoTalk preview text carries only '둘셋 · 설치 없이 바로 열려요.'
ahead.versus: Flo for Partners (fixed read-only phase and predictions), Clue (calendar dates only), 핑크다이어리 (linked calendar with item selection). A '날짜 없음' level and 'unannounced records never change his screen' were not found in any rival.

ahead.point: Quiet visuals for hard moments: a muted cover for 42 days after a loss, and no celebration visuals before a clinic confirms a positive test.
ahead.versus: The Korean pregnancy and parenting cluster is bright and baby-centred (talking baby character in 280days, point missions in 베이비빌리, daily prize events in 맘스다이어리); no quiet screen for loss or a long wait was found there. Headspace's 2024 rebrand (characters that show stress and sadness) is the benchmark for this direction.
ahead.evidence: components/cover/CoverArt.tsx (muted set), lib/logic/cover.ts, AGENTS.md '유산·임신 종료 배려' (QUIET_DAYS_AFTER_END)

ahead.point: Her home is led by the couple's own photo as a taped polaroid with 함께한 지 D+N, not by a number, a feed or an ad; the + 기록 sheet with test-strip pictograms is already finished-product quality. Caveat: the cover takes 39% of the first viewport and is a stock landscape until a photo is added.
ahead.versus: Korean cycle apps share one frame: '첫 화면에 D-day·남은 일수·예정일을 숫자로, 둘째 탭 캘린더, 그 뒤에 커뮤니티·매거진·스토어'. Flo and Natural Cycles lead with one big circle.

gaps.title: His home and the partner link are three to four screens of small text with no single hero

others.what: Oct 2025 redesign: the Today tab is built around 'One Big Thing' per day, and stacked cards were dropped for an open layout grouped by whitespace.
Home is one big cycle circle with a countdown and everything else sits below the fold; the partner gets his own mode with tailored tips, not a copy of her screen.
One screen a day: the day's question card sits at the top of home and a day's share is finished in about three minutes (from memory).
Home is a single 'today's message' card; the dad app uses the same frame with copy addressed to the father (from memory).

gaps.ours: His home is 2567px (3.04 screens) with 8 cards, 974 characters and 37 controls; his first viewport holds 323 characters against her 149. The top card (이번 달 할 일 · 정액검사 받기) is 319px with seven text blocks and its only action is a text link, 일정 보기 (components/today/MonthlyTask.tsx). The link page is 3352px with 10 cards plus 8 nested, and 4023px on first open, where a setup card asking about smoking, drinking and news fills the whole first viewport (components/link/LinkPage.tsx). Shots: ours/shots/20-him-home-vp.png and ours/shots/40-link-first-run-vp.png
gaps.gap: Nothing on his first screen is bigger than the rest: the one thing he should do is a block of 12.5px paragraphs ending in a text link, and the rest of what is his sits two to three scrolls down. On the link, his only surface and one with no push, the first open asks about his smoking and drinking before it shows him anything.
gaps.why: The promise is that he knows what to do without being chased, and today that is delivered as reading. This is cutting and re-ranking, not new features: one hero (verb, date, one filled button), two or three secondary blocks before the fold, the rest folded, and the setup questions moved after the first value on the link. It should be done before the 5-couple test (N26), or the test measures a text page instead of the idea.

gaps.title: The door he comes through has no face: text-only KakaoTalk preview, an icon that does not resolve on /link, a wordmark-only page

others.what: Designs the viewer's screen separately from the uploader's: reworked the family invite screen, added 큰글씨 모드 and a no-install web entry (2025-09) after family sign-up was low; family is now half of MAU.
No-install KakaoTalk/SMS link for the partner since 2020, plus 카카오 알림톡 notices to him (how its preview looks was not seen).
Outdoor survival-guide branding (badges, rough type, jokes) that tells a man on the first screen that this is for him (from memory, low confidence).
A separate dad app with its own name, in which a baby character speaks one line a day to the father (from memory, low confidence).

gaps.ours: app/link/layout.tsx sets openGraph title '둘셋' and description '설치 없이 바로 열려요.' with no image (health words are kept out on purpose). Icons and manifest use relative paths (app/layout.tsx:7-9) and docs/STATUS.md 2026-11-01 records a standing '/link/icon.svg' 404 on the link page. The page header is the word 둘셋 in the system font, and the cover is the stock landscape because the couple photo is not sent by default.
gaps.gap: In the chat where his wife sends it, the link is a bare title and one line with no picture, and the page behind it has no mark and no favicon or home-screen icon that resolves. The first two things he ever sees of the product carry no identity.
gaps.why: This is the cheapest high-leverage visual work in the list: one static, health-word-free OG image (mark + 둘셋), absolute icon and manifest paths so 홈 화면에 추가 gets a real icon, and the mark in the link header. It is the first impression for the person the product is positioned around and should be right before the link goes to five real husbands. The OG image needs the HTTPS host from N25 for an absolute URL.

gaps.title: Emoji stand in for people, icons and illustration next to a separate line-icon set

others.what: 2024 rebrand with rounded character illustration, a custom typeface and brand guidelines that cover colour, type, tone and motion; characters show stress and sadness as well as joy.
Bold flat illustration with one character in many expressions; widget art changes with state.
Hand-drawn pastel illustration with a talking baby character as the lead of the screen; condition input is one stamp.
Custom component library replacing hard-coded colours and sizes; logging uses simple icon tiles (tiles from memory).

gaps.ours: At least 85 distinct emoji in UI source against a consistent 56-icon line set (components/ui/icons.tsx). People are 👩 👨 🧑 in tinted circles (Avatar in components/ui/index.tsx:452, pink for the cycle owner, blue for the partner); notification rows are 🗒️ 🙏 👏 ✅ 💞; visible per screen: her home 15, 챙길 것 27, 우리 43. Shot: ours/shots/16-her-notifications-vp.png
gaps.gap: The most repeated graphic in the app, the two people, is an OS emoji that Apple, Samsung and Google each draw differently, so the look is not under our control and store screenshots cannot be made consistent. Two icon languages run side by side on every screen.
gaps.why: It is the main reason the app reads as a prototype, though it does not block the promise or the 5-couple test. The fix is small in scope: photo or initial avatars, about 20 more icons in the existing line set for notification kinds, task rows, anniversaries and baby size, and emoji kept only where a person chooses to send one (mood, reactions, signal chips). It also removes the pink/blue person code, which sits badly with the names-over-roles rule.

gaps.title: No type system: no shipped typeface, 17 sizes on one screen, half the text at 12.5px or smaller

others.what: Own typeface (Toss Product Sans, secondary claim), heavy whitespace, 'One Thing' per screen, shared TDS components.
Custom Colophon typeface as part of the 2024 rebrand.
큰글씨 모드 built for invited family viewers after family sign-up was low.
Design system as code that removed hard-coded colours and sizes; the relaunch named accessibility as the goal of the colour and calendar redesign.

gaps.ours: tailwind.config.ts:45 names Pretendard first but there is no @font-face or font file, so each phone shows its own Korean system font. Her home renders 17 sizes and 30 size×weight pairs (his 17 / 34); source has 22 arbitrary px sizes in 440 uses of text-[Npx]. 83% of the characters on her home are 13.5px or smaller and 51% are 12.5px or smaller. Sizes are fixed px and will not follow a larger system text size; weights 600/700/800 have never been checked on a real phone (docs/STATUS.md 2026-09-29).
gaps.gap: Hierarchy is carried by many near-identical sizes (12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 14.5px) instead of a few clear steps, body text is too small for a screen that asks to be read, and the wordmark and headings change shape from phone to phone.
gaps.why: A six-step scale with a 15px body floor is mechanical work across those 440 uses and also fixes Larger Text, which Apple's Accessibility Nutrition Labels now list publicly. A typeface is allowed only as a bundled, self-hosted subset (the rule bans external fonts and requires offline use), so it adds to the 366 kB first load. If that weight is not wanted, draw only the wordmark as SVG and keep system fonts on one scale. The body-size floor on his home and the link belongs with gap 1 now.

gaps.title: No ownable brand: the mark exists in two colourways, there is no wordmark, and the only illustration is a generic landscape

others.what: 2025-07 rebrand: main colour '문 블루' and a curved logo (미소·상승감).
Brand-first: dark starry theme and a circular moon-phase dashboard; the research reads it as proof that a strong visual world beats feature count for younger users.
The circular cycle wheel is the face of the brand, in a neutral design without pink or flowers (from memory).
Character-led: the couple's hand-drawn pet lives on the home screen (visual details from memory).

gaps.ours: The mark is two overlapping circles and a small dot ('둘이 셋이 되기까지', components/onboarding/WelcomeStep.tsx:22). It is blue + pink + apricot on the welcome screen but cream + tan + apricot on espresso in public/icon.svg. Inside the app and on the link the brand is the text 둘셋 in the system font. The only illustration is hills, a tree and a sun (components/cover/CoverArt.tsx). Shot: ours/shots/01-welcome-vp.png
gaps.gap: The mark has a real idea (two becoming three) but appears in two unrelated colourways and never inside the app or on the link; there is no fixed lettering and no drawing that says 'couple' or 'preparing'. Nothing would be recognised in a store grid or a chat bubble.
gaps.why: The store icon and the KakaoTalk bubble are where a couple app is first seen. Pick the espresso/cream colourway everywhere, draw 둘셋 as fixed SVG lettering, and extend the polaroid, tape and paper language (already ours) into the link header and empty states. A cute mascot is not the answer: baby-centred characters clash with the loss-aware tone. Not needed for the 5-couple test.

gaps.title: Cards have no rhythm and the same control is drawn four ways

others.what: Dropped the stacked-card layout for an open layout with whitespace grouping; detail is pushed to a second tab.
Design system as code (Compose) built specifically to remove UI inconsistency.
TDS components shared across teams, the bottom sheet as a standard component, one task per screen.
One token source with two-tier tokens (scale → semantic) feeding all platforms (low confidence).

gaps.ours: Colour is tokenised strictly (app/globals.css) but shape and spacing are not: one home has card radii of 24/22/20/12px, paddings of 18/14/16/10px, gaps of 18/14/10px and left edges at 16, 18 and 20–25px. Cards differ from the page by 1.05:1, so the shadow does all the separating. Checks have four looks (circle right, circle left, square box, bordered row), the primary button is a pill on home and a 12px rectangle in sheets, the link page uses up to six pastel tints, and tab order changes by stage (components/ui/index.tsx, components/AppShell.tsx).
gaps.gap: There are tokens for colour but none for radius, spacing or control shape, so every screen is a stack of slightly different boxes. This is what separates 'carefully made prototype' from 'finished product' at a glance.
gaps.why: Once decided it is mechanical: two radii, one card padding, one check, one primary button, fewer cards grouped by whitespace and titles. Start on his home and the link together with gap 1, then sweep the rest before any store screenshot is taken.

gaps.title: The welcome screen and everything store-facing do not show the product

others.what: A very long personalised quiz in which each answer visibly changes what comes next, with the paywall only after it; the home it lands on is one big cycle circle.
Onboarding run like a health consultation rather than a setup form.
Mascot-led chat onboarding; the mascot speaks the first run.
Picked as Apple '투데이의 앱' in 2025-05; the company cites intuitive UI/UX and stage-matched information.

gaps.ours: Welcome is a polaroid landscape, mark + 둘셋, one line with sub-copy and 시작하기; it shows no view of his screen, the link or a first week, and the lower ~150px is empty (components/onboarding/WelcomeStep.tsx). There are no store screenshots, landing page, marketing visuals or brand guidelines. Product screens still carry prototype furniture (the demo-date banner and the ⇄ viewer pill), and the demo data includes a cheer line that breaks our own copy rules (lib/demo.ts:709: '벌써 사흘째 둘 다 체크했어요! … 🌙').
gaps.gap: Of the screens today, her home with a real photo could pass as a store screenshot; his home, the one that carries the positioning, could not. The welcome says '남편이 같이 하는 임신 준비' in words and shows a hill.
gaps.why: It is a launch requirement, but it should come after gaps 1, 3, 5 and 6, otherwise the screenshots are of screens that will change. Do not copy the 30-to-55-step quiz: our 4-decision first run is a strength. Show his side and hers together on the welcome, and clean the demo data so store shots follow the copy rules (no streak-like '사흘째', no exclamation mark, no decorative emoji).

gaps.title: Nothing visual accumulates on his side; the rivals' answer is a mascot or a streak, which we ban

others.what: A shared virtual pet on the home screen works as a shared streak with a visible penalty (it grows, or turns to stone).
State-based character art (panicked when not done, relaxed when done) and custom streak-milestone celebration animations.
Consecutive-day count, and past answers pile up as a timeline that becomes the couple's asset (from memory).
A realistic 3D fetal model at the top of home that changes every week as the daily thing to look at (from memory).

gaps.ours: What builds up for him is the '내 준비' bar (about-3-month timer, 이번 주 N/7, test chain; components/today/MyPrepBar.tsx, lib/logic/myPrep.ts) and a '고마워했어요' line that lasts the week (lib/logic/weekTogether.ts). Weeks with nothing done are deliberately not shown; streaks, badges and rankings are non-goals (docs/positioning.md §6).
gaps.gap: After a month his screen looks the same as on day one: a thin bar and lines of text. The rivals fill this place with a growing character or a counter; we were right to ban both, but nothing visual has taken their place.
gaps.why: With no push and no streak, what he sees when he does come back has to carry more weight than in the rival apps. Pre-pregnancy there is no baby or week clock to draw, so the picture has to come from what the two of them have done. Decide the exact form after the 5-couple test, but it can double as the hero graphic that gap 1 needs.
gaps.instead: A record that only ever adds: draw the about-3-month prep timer as an arc that fills for any week in which he did something, never empties and never shows gaps; and keep her [고마워요] and his finished steps (신청 → 검사 → 청구) as small stamped marks. No consecutive-day number, no penalty or 'missed' state, paused during the 42 quiet days, and nothing of his smoking, drinking or medicine rows named on her side.

gaps.title: The 주기 tab opens on text, the cycle is drawn small, and his side shows it in three different shapes

others.what: Home is one big cycle circle with a countdown; insights are placed so they never clutter the circle (Flo design team).
One circular cycle wheel shows period, fertile window and PMS on home (from memory); the relaunch rebuilt the calendar for accessibility.
A horizontal date strip marks period and fertile days as red and light-blue ovals, with log items listed below (from memory).
A row of test-strip photos and the LH curve stacked on one screen.

gaps.ours: The home ring (components/today/CycleRing.tsx) is about 80px with 10px labels. The 주기 tab's first viewport is a switch row and a violet card with a title, a paragraph and four label/value pairs; the 달력 heading starts at y=734 and the month grid is under the tab bar (components/tabs/CycleTab.tsx; shot ours/shots/11-her-cycle-vp.png). The calendar needs a six-swatch legend, cycle history is a list with no cycle-length bars or LH series, and his side draws the same window as a week row on home, a tinted month on 주기 and a 7-day row on the link.
gaps.gap: A tab called 주기 shows no cycle until she scrolls, and past cycles are never drawn at all. To someone with years in a calendar-first tracker it reads as a report, and the benchmark rule of one consistent cycle shape across her view and his is not met.
gaps.why: Putting the calendar first, shrinking the summary to one line and enlarging the ring is a small reorder. Trend charts should stay light and come later: positioning §5 says not to fight the tracker she already uses, and a daily chance score or exact ovulation day is ruled out. Simple cycle-length bars from her own history are enough after launch.

gaps.title: Almost no motion and no designed completion moment

others.what: Months spent tuning slider feel, fingertip haptic ticks and animation smoothness for a scrubbable cycle (ADA 2026 Interaction winner per the research).
Strong visual feedback on completing a small goal.
Motion is part of the brand guidelines alongside colour, type and tone.
Custom celebration animations at streak milestones.

gaps.ours: There are no @keyframes of our own; the only motion is CSS transitions (check fill 120ms, progress bar 500ms, switch knob) and one loading pulse. Sheets, toasts and tab changes appear at once (Sheet and ToastProvider in components/ui/index.tsx). Finishing all checks gives a green line and a toast; there are no haptics. prefers-reduced-motion is already respected.
gaps.gap: His [했어요] and her [고마워요], the two moments the weekly loop exists for, look the same as flipping a setting, and sheets that pop instead of slide make the app feel like a web page.
gaps.why: Sheet and toast enter/exit and a drawn check are a few CSS keyframes; one calm, designed moment when [고마워요] arrives is the part worth care. Do not copy Duolingo's streak celebrations, and keep the existing rules: nothing before a clinic confirms, nothing in the 42 quiet days, no auto-praise text. Real haptics have to wait for the Capacitor wrap, because iOS Safari has no vibration API.

gaps.title: Pregnancy and baby stages have no picture of the stage

others.what: Weekly baby illustration and information, built around the clinic's ultrasound video.
A talking baby character is the lead of the screen; 'what the baby said today' is the reason to open.
A realistic 3D fetal model for the week at the top of home (from memory).
Compares baby size to objects men know instead of fruit (from memory, low confidence).

gaps.ours: Pregnancy is a week count and a progress bar; baby size is a citrus emoji in a box; the baby is a 👧 emoji (components/pregnancy/WeekCard.tsx; design audit 'Stage heroes have no picture of the stage'). These stages are kept minimal by decision (docs/positioning.md).
gaps.gap: When a couple succeeds, the first screen of the new stage is the emotional high point and it is a progress bar and a fruit emoji.
gaps.why: The core user is the preparing couple, and the leaders' ultrasound video and 3D models are not something a one-or-two-person team should chase. The cheap version is to replace the stage emoji with a small set of line drawings as part of gap 3; anything richer waits until couples actually reach this stage in the app.

gaps.title: No theme choice in the app, and two hot spots in dark

others.what: Dark mode toggle in the app: Menu > Settings > Appearance.
Discreet app icons and a discreet widget view on iOS.
Dark-first UI as the brand itself.

gaps.ours: The theme follows prefers-color-scheme only (app/globals.css:54) and 설정 has no switch. In dark, the salmon demo cover and the cream FAB are the brightest objects on the screen (ours/shots/10-her-home-dark-vp.png). The app name and icon already carry no health words, and lock-screen text hiding exists.
gaps.gap: Someone who wants dulset dark on a light phone, or the reverse, cannot have it, and the dark home pulls the eye to the + button and the cover instead of the status card.
gaps.why: Dark mode itself is a strength; this is polish. A three-way switch (시스템 / 밝게 / 어둡게) is a token swap because themes are already CSS variables. An alternate discreet icon needs the native wrap and matters less here because our icon and name are already discreet.

analysis.notes:
Evidence quality: almost every rival's colours, illustration and home layout in the input are from researcher memory or store-text summaries; no rival screenshot was seen in the research. The design-benchmarks cluster (Flo, Oura, Clue, Toss, Headspace, Duolingo) is the best-sourced, so the gaps lean on it. I cannot claim a like-for-like visual comparison with 핑크다이어리, 해피문데이 or 베이비빌리. Our own screenshots are headless Chromium with a fallback font (WenQuanYi Zen Hei + Inter), so Korean glyph shapes differ from a real iPhone or Galaxy.

Screenshots opened (8 of 8 allowed), all under ours/shots/: 10-her-home-vp.png, 20-him-home-vp.png, 40-link-first-run-vp.png, 11-her-cycle-vp.png, 01-welcome-vp.png, 10-her-home-dark-vp.png, 16-her-notifications-vp.png, 21-him-cycle-vp.png. WebSearch used: 0 of 3; no hole decided a critical gap.

Confirmed in code today: Pretendard is named at tailwind.config.ts:45 with no @font-face in app/globals.css; app/link/layout.tsx has OG title and description but no image; the mark's two colourways (components/onboarding/WelcomeStep.tsx:22 against public/icon.svg); avatar tone is set by tracksCycle (components/ui/index.tsx:452); the demo cheer line at lib/demo.ts:709. The '/link/icon.svg' 404 comes from docs/STATUS.md (2026-11-01 hand-off) plus the relative icon paths in app/layout.tsx; I did not load the page myself, and that the home-screen icon also fails on /link is an inference from the same relative path.

Severity calls that differ from the internal design audit: the audit rates emoji-as-icons critical; I rate it major, because it blocks store-grade screenshots but not the promise or the 5-couple test. Only the husband's screens are critical here.

Suggested order: gaps 1 and 2 now, with the body-size floor from gap 4 on his home and the link; then 6, 4, 3, 5; store screenshots and welcome (7) last, because they depend on the others. Gap 8 is the one that conflicts with the product rules and should be decided after N26.

Left out on purpose: home-screen and lock-screen widgets and watch faces (Duolingo, Finch, 더데이비포, 베이비빌리, 베이비타임) are a delivery-surface gap that needs the native wrap and belongs to the platform dimension; for design it only means keeping one cycle shape and one 'this week' unit that a widget could reuse. Tablet and desktop layouts are not a gap for this product.

checked.ours_note: Mostly holds, but 'nothing on his first screen is bigger than the rest' is overstated. In shots/20-him-home-vp.png the largest thing is the couple polaroid cover (about 300px, components/today/CoverHero.tsx), and the task title '정액검사 받기' is clearly bigger than the body text. So the problem is that the cover outranks his task, and the task card (components/today/MonthlyTask.tsx) is seven text blocks with a text link '일정 보기' and no filled button. On the link, shots/40-link-first-run-vp.png confirms the setup card (smoking, drinking, news, with 건너뛰기 and 나중에 할게요) fills the whole first viewport before he sees anything (components/link/LinkPage.tsx).
checked.rival_note: Saved sources cover Oura's Oct 2025 'One Big Thing' Today tab and dropped card layout (9to5google, TechCrunch), Flo's circle-countdown main screen (help.flo.health), and Flo for Partners' tailored tips (flo.health newsroom). Paired's daily framing has an official article ('5 minutes a day'), but 'one card at the top of home' is still memory. For パパninaru, the JP App Store shows daily advice for men; the single-card home layout is not confirmed.
checked.reason_if_changed: Do it now, but rate it major rather than critical. His task is already in the first viewport with a readable title, and the link setup card can be skipped and is about his own screen, so nothing is broken; it is a ranking problem. The fix should also move or shrink the cover on his home (the analysis does not mention it), not only the task card.

analysis.standing: dulset's interaction basics are sound and in places better than the leaders': a first run with 4 required decisions and value on the first home, one logging sheet with tap-to-save and 되돌리기, calm error states, and measured contrast and labelling. analysis.notes:
Evidence limits. No rival screen was seen by the research (profiles rest on search summaries and memory; several are low confidence), so comparisons on rivals' motion, undo, empty and error states are thin. Where a rival behaviour was 'not found' I did not treat it as absent. Our own numbers come from headless Chromium at 390×844 with a fallback font and a demo couple; nothing was timed with people, on a real phone, or with a screen reader.

What I checked myself. I opened 7 of our screenshots: 20-him-home-vp, 40-link-first-run-vp, 41-link-page-vp, 10-her-home-vp, 11-her-cycle-vp, 01-welcome-vp, 79-after-period-log-toast-vp. Code checks on 2026-11-13: no navigator.vibrate anywhere; loading is a pulsing text label at components/AppShell.tsx:39 and components/link/LinkPage.tsx:508; the reduced-motion rule is at app/globals.css:228; the link's offline line and notices are at LinkPage.tsx:490 and LinkNotice.tsx; '되돌리기' appears in 14 component files; there is no auto-tell setting. No WebSearch was used (0 of 3).

Overlap with other dimensions. design-ux-1 (push) and the mock transport are also platform gaps; here they are judged only as the return path of the loop. Type scale, emoji-as-icons, brand and card rhythm belong to the visual-design dimension; I used them only where they change use (reading size, his text-heavy screens).

Considered and not listed as gaps:
- A long personalisation quiz (Flo 30-55 steps, Natural Cycles ~31): it serves their paywall, and our short first run is better for this product.
- 'Set once and the app tells him' (ケアミー, ペアケア): a partner-feature question. A standing choice made by her would fit 'the owner decides', but positioning §6 excludes automatic peak sending.
- A daily probability score as the home hero: a medical-claim conflict that belongs to the features dimension.
- Home layout personalisation and search: these exist mainly because rivals are larger.
- An in-app theme switch: polish, folded into design-ux-7.

Smaller defects folded in or left out: four different check styles and native date inputs (consistency), empty states that are functional only, the cover cropping to a ~60px strip at 375×667, and the consent step's second checkbox below the fold (mentioned in design-ux-4).

Sequencing. design-ux-2, -3 and -4 are cheap and should land before the 5-couple validation, otherwise it measures a questionnaire and a wall of text rather than the idea. design-ux-6 (service worker) is the prerequisite for the first step of design-ux-1.

analysis.dimension: Content, expert review, community and AI assistant
analysis.standing: dulset's content is a dated, sourced checklist (61 roadmap items, 10 programme cards, 12 habit/supplement notes, 5 guide sections) with no editorial library; it has no article or video feed, no community, no expert Q&A, no AI and no named medical reviewer, and 84 of 196 audited entries are still flagged unverified. Rivals in Korea and abroad treat doctor-reviewed content plus a community as standard furniture, and generative AI chat is only now arriving (2026). What dulset has that they do not is partner-side content that is a task with a date and passes her sharing choice; its weak points are trust (no review, unverified husband items) and how little new there is for the husband to read or see before pregnancy.

ahead.point: Every roadmap and programme item carries source URLs, an effective date and a checked date, and an unverified item says so on screen ('공식 안내에서 한 번 더 확인해 주세요'); a validator checks sources, dates and banned words before every test run.

analysis.standing: dulset is strong on privacy that is built into the structure and weak on everything an outsider could check. analysis.notes:
No WebSearch was used (0 of 3); the input and targeted greps were enough.

Confirmed in the repo this run:
- The link's first run has no consent step and sends his habit answers ('setup' event).
- 설정 › 정보 has no operator name or contact.
- The link can be made only on the cycle owner's phone.
- No code, PIN or device binding on the link was found.
- No delivery state for her signals was found.

- PARTNER_WEEKLY_CAP is 2, and the link layout is noindex.

Deliberately not listed as gaps, because they exist only through rivals' size or fall outside this dimension:
- store ratings and review counts, user numbers, ISO/ISMS-P certification, press and awards;

Overlap to expect with other dimensions: trust-business-1 (no push), trust-business-2 (mock transport) and trust-business-9 (no accounts) are platform facts; they are listed here for their retention, growth and trust consequences.

Caveats:
- The legal points in trust-business-3 to 5 (a published policy, each person's consent for sensitive data, an age limit, the medical-device boundary) are a product reading, not legal advice; the legal review listed in N18 should confirm them.
- The iOS web-push and in-app-browser limits in trust-business-1 are from memory.

- The research open-counter needs a line in the policy and in his consent, even though it holds only couple id, date and count.
